Shivakumar alleged that the forms were being used to target voters from minority, Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe and backward-class communities. items.title: One Nation, One Election: Supreme Court says no parliamentary panel meeting with CJI, judges
items.summary: The Supreme Court of India has said that no meeting will take place between its judges and the Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC) examining the 'One Nation, One Election' bills. Sources at the Supreme Court revealed the same to Bar & Bench hours after Senior Advocate Kapil Sibal said at a press conference that the JPC was scheduled to hold discussions with the Chief Justice of India (CJI) and other apex court judges on October 6. According to PTI , the JPC dropped the plan to meet top court judges after the opposition raised objections to the same. The JPC, chaired by BJP Member of Parliament PP Chaudhary, is examining the Constitution (One Hundred and Twenty-Ninth Amendment) Bill, 2024 and the Union Territories Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2024. The two bills seek to put in place a framework for holding Lok Sabha and State Assembly elections together. Senior Advocate Kapil Sibal Sibal termed the proposed interaction unprecedented and unconstitutional. He said that a parliamentary committee briefing sitting judges on a bill, even before finalising its report, has never happened in India's history. items.title: How HCU’s Left-Ambedkarite alliance overturned previous ABVP sweep in student polls
items.summary: The University of Hyderabad’s student union election has ended with a result that, on the surface, looks like a reversal of last year. The left-leaning AISA-ASA-DSU-SFI-TSF alliance has won all four executive positions for 2026-27, along with the cultural secretary post. The right-wing ABVP-SLVD (Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad – Sevalal Vidyarthi Dal) panel retained only the sports secretary post. The elections took place on September 28 and the results were declared the next day. But the result is not simply a Left-Ambedkarite victory over the ABVP. It is also the reversal of the political conditions that produced ABVP’s sweeping victory in 2025. Last year, ABVP-SLVD won all six major posts, returning to power after seven years. A major factor was the split between the Students’ Federation of India (SFI) and the Ambedkar Students’ Association (ASA), two organisations that had together helped keep ABVP out of power since 2019. The two had disagreed over the inclusion of Muslim student organisations, while the Congress-affiliated NSUI also faced student dissatisfaction over the university’s land issue, according to reporting at the time. items.title: The Act notification veto: When 'when' quietly becomes 'never'
items.summary: Once a bill gets the President's assent, most people assume that's the end of the story. Fewer stop to ask the second question: when does it actually start applying? For at least 3 Indian statutes, no one has given a real answer to that in years. In one case, it's been more than 3 decades. Take the Delhi Rent Act. The President assented to it on August 23, 1995, but it has remained uncommenced ever since. This is because the decision on this lies with a Central government notification under Section 1(3) , which has not been made in over three decades now. Advocate Shobha Aggarwal took the matter to court in 2025 . A law that never lived Parliament passed the Act. It was signed by the President; then it lay there, as nothing in the statute obliged the government to justify itself in any time frame. The Delhi Rent Act, 1995 is, therefore, now an Act that is on the statute book but not implemented to this day, waiting for a notification “on such date as the Central government may appoint.” And this is not an isolated incident. items.title: CIRP under IBC can continue even if insolvency plea that triggered it was fraudulent: Supreme Court
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Wednesday held that a corporate insolvency resolution process (CIRP) under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC) can continue even if the insolvency application that originally triggered the process is subsequently found to have been fraudulent and collusive [Orris Vs Rakesh Kumar Gupta]. A Bench of Justices PS Narasimha and Alok Aradhe held that while the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) has the power to recall the admission of an insolvency application obtained through fraud, such a finding does not automatically require the entire CIRP to be terminated. “ The initiating creditor is merely the triggering creditor, and not the proprietor of the CIRP, ” the judgment said. Once an insolvency application is admitted, the proceedings cease to remain a dispute between the creditor who initiated the process and the corporate debtor. They become proceedings in rem involving the entire body of creditors and other stakeholders, the Court explained. “ The resolution process can therefore continue even in the absence of the original applicant, ” the top court made it clear. items.summary: The Bombay High Court at Goa on Thursday expressed concern about the manner in which Election Commission of India's (ECI) automated software system rejects form 8 applications filed by electors to report a change of address [Paresh Salgaonkar & Ors v. State of Goa & Ors.] Under the automated system, form 8 applications are rejected if the applicant fails to submit a pre-filled enumeration form at their previous residence. The Court remarked that while the ECI’s protocol successfully purges non-resident entries, it fails to achieve its corresponding goal of enumerating shifted voters. The Bench also noted that rejection orders cited "system glitches," indicating the portal gave officers no choice but to reject form 8 filings. The Court also took exception to the ECI invoking public perception and confidence in the electoral exercise to support the commission's revision framework. The Bench rebuked the ECI and made it clear that court proceedings are governed strictly by legal provisions rather than external opinion and public sentiment should not be a ground to bypass the law. “What the public thinks about all of us is immaterial. items.title: Common knowledge that data of Indians is traded on dark web: Supreme Court
items.summary: It is common knowledge that personal data of Indians is traded on the dark web, the Supreme Court said on Thursday. A Bench of Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana was hearing a plea moved by cybersecurity researcher Himanshu Pathak regarding alleged data vulnerabilities in the systems of Star Health and Allied Insurance Company. Justice Joymalya Bagchi, Justice V Mohana Representing Star Health, Senior Advocate S Muralidhar today assured the Court that the data being secured by the insurance company is secure, contrary to Pathak’s apprehensions. “ We have taken extraordinary security measures. Your Lordships will be quite astonished how many layers of security we have built. We do continuous monitoring now , ” Muralidhar said. “ But it is common knowledge that data of Indians is being traded on the dark web ,” pointed out Justice Bagchi. “ Dark web is something beyond the control of anyone, with the greatest respect. Just because there is a dark web, we cannot be complicit,” replied Muralidhar. Senior Advocate S Muralidhar Advocate Prashant Bhushan appeared for Pathak. items.title: Kerala electricity crisis: Himachal Pradesh signs deal with KSEB, offers temporary relief
items.summary: The Congress-led government in Himachal Pradesh has come to the rescue of its counterpart in Kerala, which has been facing a major electricity crisis since it assumed power in May this year. Following negotiations with officials of Kerala State Electricity Board (KSEB), the Himachal Pradesh government has agreed to provide Kerala 600–900 MW of electricity from October 1 onwards. This is expected to be sufficient to meet the peak demand of the state. A deficient monsoon coupled with a high power consumption had disrupted KSEB’s power distribution from June to September. A senior officer of KSEB said that the purchase from Himachal Pradesh was enough to avoid the existing power curbs. In addition to the agreement with Himachal, KSEB has also managed to secure certain short term deals of around 450-500 MW. It is currently unclear whether KSEB will continue purchasing from Himachal Pradesh, though it is seeking an agreement to extend the arrangement for the next few months. KSEB is also relieved that the electricity it had to return as part of ‘swap’ agreement with other states ended by September 30.
